summary: Biography of Iranian general Qassem Soleimani, from poor boy in Kerman to Quds Force chief who ran Iran's proxy wars in Iraq, Syria and beyond, set against decades of US meddling until his 2020 assassination.

evidence.note: birth in 1957 in a Kerman Province village
joins the new Revolutionary Guard after the 1979 revolution
sent to crush the Kurdish uprising at Mahabad
front-line service through the Iran-Iraq War
US secretly arming both Iran and Iraq, intelligence for chemical attacks
eastern drug war and anti-Taliban support in Afghanistan
Axis of Evil speech ends Iran-US cooperation in Afghanistan
Quds Force EFPs and jihadi pipelines against US troops in Iraq
Shia militias propping up Assad in the Syrian Civil War
state-built cult of personality and martyrdom image
live news of Iranian missile strikes after the assassination

notes: Primary theme chosen as war-war-crimes because most airtime is Soleimani's wars and proxy campaigns; the taxonomy lists this story as an example of diplomacy-foreign-policy, so reviewers may prefer to swap the two. Pahlavi-era Iran has no polity id. US placed last in setting as the policy actor rather than harm site.
